findings.message: Custom class loader does not call its superclass's getPermissions()
findings.description: Custom class loader org.eclipse.jetty.ee.webapp.WebAppClassLoader.getPermissions(CodeSource) does not call its superclass's getPermissions()

tool_specific.details: SEI CERT rule SEC07-J requires that custom class loaders must always call their superclass's getPermissions() method in their own getPermissions() method to initialize the object they return at the end. Omitting it means that a class defined using this custom class loader has permissions that are completely independent of those specified in the systemwide policy file. In effect, the class's permissions override them.

findings.message: Equals checks for incompatible operand
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.http.spi.JettyHttpExchange.equals(Object) checks for operand being a JettyHttpExchangeDelegate

tool_specific.details: This equals method is checking to see if the argument is some incompatible type (i.e., a class that is neither a supertype nor subtype of the class that defines the equals method). For example, the Foo class might have an equals method that looks like: public boolean equals(Object o) { if (o instanceof Foo) return name.equals(((Foo)o).name); else if (o instanceof String) return name.equals(o); else return false; } This is considered bad practice, as it makes it very hard to implement an equals method that is symmetric and transitive. Without those properties, very unexpected behaviors are possible.

findings.message: May expose internal static state by storing a mutable object into a static field
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.http.spi.JettyHttpServerProvider.setServer(Server) may expose internal static state by storing a mutable object into a static field org.eclipse.jetty.http.spi.JettyHttpServerProvider._server

tool_specific.details: This code stores a reference to an externally mutable object into a static field. If unchecked changes to the mutable object would compromise security or other important properties, you will need to do something different. Storing a copy of the object is better approach in many situations.

findings.message: Comparison of String parameter using == or !=
findings.description: Comparison of String parameter using == or != in org.eclipse.jetty.http.HttpCookie.equalsIgnoreCase(String, String)

tool_specific.details: This code compares a java.lang.String parameter for reference equality using the == or != operators. Requiring callers to pass only String constants or interned strings to a method is unnecessarily fragile, and rarely leads to measurable performance gains. Consider using the equals(Object) method instead. See CWE-595: Comparison of Object References Instead of Object Contents.

findings.message: Operation on shared variable is not atomic
findings.description: Operation on the "_length" shared variable in "HttpParser" class is not atomic

tool_specific.details: This write of a variable shared between functions depends on the current value of the variable (either because it's a compound operation - e.g. +=, ++ - or it simply depends on the current value), as such it consists of more than one discrete operation. These operations are not atomic in themselves and need further synchronization. See SEI CERT rule VNA02-J, CWE-366: Race Condition within a Thread, CWE-413: Improper Resource Locking, CWE-567: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context, and CWE-667: Improper Locking. Simply declaring a variable volatile fails to guarantee the atomicity of compound operations on the variable, but synchronizing the writes on top of declaring the variable volatile for read operations is sufficient. To solve this issue, synchronize compound operations and other write operations depending on the previous value, use read-write locks, or declare the shared variable with an atomic type.

findings.message: Format string should use %n rather than \n
findings.description: Format string should use %n rather than \n in org.eclipse.jetty.http.HttpTester$Response.toString()

tool_specific.details: This format string includes a newline character (\n). In format strings, it is generally preferable to use %n, which will produce the platform-specific line separator. When using text blocks introduced in Java 15, use the \ escape sequence: String value = """ first line%n\ second line%n\ """;

findings.message: Negating the result of compareTo()/compare()
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.http.QuotedQualityCSV$QualityValue.compareTo(QuotedQualityCSV$QualityValue) negates the return value of Integer.compare(int, int)

tool_specific.details: This code negates the return value of a compareTo or compare method. This is a questionable or bad programming practice, since if the return value is Integer.MIN_VALUE, negating the return value won't negate the sign of the result. You can achieve the same intended result by reversing the order of the operands rather than by negating the results.

findings.message: Field should be package protected
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.http3.qpack.internal.metadata.Http3Fields.STATUSES should be package protected

tool_specific.details: A mutable static field could be changed by malicious code or by accident. The field could be made package protected to avoid this vulnerability. See CWE-607: Public Static Final Field References Mutable Object.

findings.message: Class names shouldn't shadow simple name of implemented interface
findings.description: The class name org.eclipse.jetty.jndi.InitialContextFactory shadows the simple name of implemented interface javax.naming.spi.InitialContextFactory

tool_specific.details: This class/interface has a simple name that is identical to that of an implemented/extended interface, except that the interface is in a different package (e.g., alpha.Foo extends beta.Foo). This can be exceptionally confusing, create lots of situations in which you have to look at import statements to resolve references and creates many opportunities to accidentally define methods that do not override methods in their superclasses.

findings.message: Method may fail to close stream
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.maven.AbstractForkedChild.loadWebAppProps() may fail to close stream

tool_specific.details: The method creates an IO stream object, does not assign it to any fields, pass it to other methods that might close it, or return it, and does not appear to close the stream on all paths out of the method. This may result in a file descriptor leak. It is generally a good idea to use a finally block to ensure that streams are closed. See CWE-459: Incomplete Cleanup.

findings.message: Field isn't final but should be
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.maven.MavenServerConnector.PORT_SYSPROPERTY isn't final but should be

tool_specific.details: This public static or protected static field is not final, and could be changed by malicious code or by accident from another package. The field could be made final to avoid this vulnerability. See CWE-500: Public Static Field Not Marked Final.

findings.message: Field is a mutable collection which should be package protected
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.maven.SelectiveJarResource.DEFAULT_INCLUDES is a mutable collection which should be package protected

tool_specific.details: A mutable collection instance is assigned to a static final field, thus can be changed by malicious code or by accident from another package. The field could be made package protected to avoid this vulnerability. Alternatively you may wrap this field into Collections.unmodifiableSet/List/Map/etc. to avoid this vulnerability.

findings.message: Method invokes System.exit(...)
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.server.ShutdownService$ShutdownRunnable.run() invokes System.exit(...), which shuts down the entire virtual machine

tool_specific.details: Invoking System.exit shuts down the entire Java virtual machine. This should only been done when it is appropriate. Such calls make it hard or impossible for your code to be invoked by other code. Consider throwing a RuntimeException instead. See CWE-382: J2EE Bad Practices: Use of System.exit().

findings.message: Random object created and used only once
findings.description: Random object created and used only once in org.eclipse.jetty.session.DefaultSessionIdManager.initRandom()

tool_specific.details: This code creates a java.util.Random object, uses it to generate one random number, and then discards the Random object. This produces mediocre quality random numbers and is inefficient. If possible, rewrite the code so that the Random object is created once and saved, and each time a new random number is required invoke a method on the existing Random object to obtain it. If it is important that the generated Random numbers not be guessable, you must not create a new Random for each random number; the values are too easily guessable. You should strongly consider using a java.security.SecureRandom instead (and avoid allocating a new SecureRandom for each random number needed).

findings.message: Method with Boolean return type returns explicit null
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.logging.JettyLoggerConfiguration.lambda$getHideStacks$0(String) has Boolean return type and returns explicit null

tool_specific.details: A method that returns either Boolean.TRUE, Boolean.FALSE or null is an accident waiting to happen. This method can be invoked as though it returned a value of type boolean, and the compiler will insert automatic unboxing of the Boolean value. If a null value is returned, this will result in a NullPointerException.

findings.message: Method does not release lock on all exception paths
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.util.Blocker$Shared$1.close() does not release lock on all exception paths

tool_specific.details: This method acquires a JSR-166 (java.util.concurrent) lock, but does not release it on all exception paths out of the method. In general, the correct idiom for using a JSR-166 lock is: Lock l = ...; l.lock(); try { // do something } finally { l.unlock(); } See CWE-413: Improper Resource Locking and CWE-459: Incomplete Cleanup.

findings.message: Iterator next() method cannot throw NoSuchElementException
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.util.BlockingArrayQueue$Itr.next() cannot throw NoSuchElementException

tool_specific.details: This class implements the java.util.Iterator interface. However, its next() method is not capable of throwing java.util.NoSuchElementException. The next() method should be changed so it throws NoSuchElementException if is called when there are no more elements to return.

findings.message: Class is not derived from an Exception, even though it is named as such
findings.description: Class org.eclipse.jetty.util.ExceptionUtil$MultiException is not derived from an Exception, even though it is named as such

tool_specific.details: This class is not derived from another exception, but ends with 'Exception'. This will be confusing to users of this class.

findings.message: Class implements Cloneable but does not define or use clone method
findings.description: Class org.eclipse.jetty.util.LazyList implements Cloneable but does not define or use clone method

tool_specific.details: Class implements Cloneable but does not define or use the clone method.

findings.message: Comparator doesn't implement Serializable
findings.description: org.eclipse.jetty.util.TopologicalSort$InitialOrderComparator implements Comparator but not Serializable

tool_specific.details: This class implements the Comparator interface. You should consider whether or not it should also implement the Serializable interface. If a comparator is used to construct an ordered collection such as a TreeMap, then the TreeMap will be serializable only if the comparator is also serializable. As most comparators have little or no state, making them serializable is generally easy and good defensive programming. See CWE-1066: Missing Serialization Control Element.
